title: SRE gemba-walk notes: rotation observations and quick fixes
content:
Context:
This doc is a set of hand-scribbled notes from a week of "gemba" style shadowing and on-call pairing across three rotations (UTC nights + PST mornings) in the last sprint. Goal: surface low-effort operational wins and recurring friction points that show up during live incidents and handoffs. Not a polished postmortem — think: quick observations, tiny experiments to try, and owners for follow-ups.

Who I shadowed / sessions:
- 2027-02-14 22:00-02:00 UTC: paired with Evan (night rotation) — primary paging window for EU region.
- 2027-02-16 07:30-10:00 PST: morning handoff with Maya + ops triage.
- 2027-02-17 23:45-01:30 UTC: incident replay with Ravi (pager-to-bridge handoff).

High-level patterns observed (quick):
- Alert fatigue cluster: ~40% of page noise in the night window is from duplicate downstream requeue spikes (kafka consumer lag alert + downstream 5xx) — same underlying cause but separate alerts cascade.
- Handoff blurriness: morning notes often lack explicit 'what I'm watching' lines. Handoff doc sections exist but are freeform; on-call assumes mental context.
- Runbook friction: the latency runbook requires a model-specific metric name mapping step; not all models have the mapping updated in the doc. People copy/paste and introduce small errors under pressure.
- SLO burn visibility inconsistent: on-call dashboards show SLO burn but not rolling 12h projected burn rate easily (we look for 3-, 6-, 12-hour projections).
- Quiet-hours edge cases: scheduled maintenance windows during low traffic still trigger escalation paths because alerting rules don't check the maintenance flag consistently.

Concrete incidents seen or replayed (notes):
1) 2027-02-14 23:10 UTC - EU inference region slowdowns
- Symptom: p95 gen latency increased by ~1.6x for ~12 minutes, error rate stable.
- Root cause (probable): a burst of cold-starts from a batch job that restarted a shard; autoscaler had a delayed scale due to a bug in scaling cooldown logic.
- Pain: paging noise included autoscaler, host-health, and application-layer latency alerts.
- Near-term: suppress autoscaler alert when host-health is the initial signal OR add an initial triage checklist to the page.
- Owner: Evan — ticket JIRA-SRE-7894 to add suppression rule and add to autoscaler playbook.

2) 2027-02-17 00:05 UTC - Tokenization/embedding job causing downstream queue pressure
- Symptom: queue depth + worker 429 spikes; customer-facing endpoints saw elevated retries.
- Quick fix used: revert throttling config on worker pool so backpressure was applied earlier, preventing head-of-line blocking.
- Follow-up: add dedicated throttling policy for batch embedding jobs; schedule a debug-run in staging during off-hours.
- Owner: Maya — follow-up doc and staging run by 2027-03-04.

Operational suggestions (low-effort experiments):
- Consolidate chained alerts into a single 'incident parent' for common failure classes. Quick wins: kafka-lag -> downstream-5xx grouping; autoscaler events -> scale-latency. (Owner: Priya, due 2027-03-01)
- Introduce a one-line "watchlist" in the handoff template: 3 bullets max (what I'm watching, known gotchas, outstanding mitigations). Make it required in the morning handoff Slack stub. (Owner: Ravi, due 2027-02-25)
- Add a 12h burn-rate projection chart to the SLO dashboard (prototype: existing SLO dashboard + linear regression on the last 12h window). If projection > 0.3 (30% of budget in 12h), auto-open a high-level bridging channel for async triage. (Owner: Liam, prototype by 2027-03-08)
- Quick runbook edits: add a 'model mapping' quick table at the top of latency runbook and a small verification step (copy-paste-proof). (Owner: Priya + eng-ml-modeling reviewer, due 2027-02-28)

Handoff checklist (proposed minimal template):
- Current watchlist (3 bullets)
- Active incidents (IDs + 1-line status)
- Scheduled maintenance windows (times + affected clusters)
- Known noisy alerts to ignore (with exact alert name)
- Outstanding mitigations (owner + ETA)

Runbook and tooling gaps noted:
- Missing example commands for 'force-evict' vs 'soft-drain' on nodes. People used different flags and some used deprecated commands (we should canonicalize).
- Playbook for 'cascade suppression' exists but needs a clear decision table: when to suppress downstream alerts vs when to escalate.
- No easy way in Slack stub to show 'escalation history' — ops would like the last 3 page recipients included automatically by the pager.

Small follow-ups / action items (owners & dates):
- Priya: Draft alert grouping RFC and sample suppression rules (2027-03-01).
- Evan: Patch autoscaler cooldown logic test + add canary on staging (2027-02-25).
- Maya: Batch embedding throttling policy doc + staging test (2027-03-04).
- Ravi: Update handoff template and push Slack stub change (2027-02-25).
- Liam: Prototype 12h SLO burn projection visualization (2027-03-08).

Open questions / unresolved bits:
- Should we prefer suppression or improved routing when alerts cascade? Tradeoffs: suppression reduces noise but hides secondary signals; routing surfaces impact but increases pages. Need a decision framework.
- What is the acceptable interruption budget for night rotation? Ops asks for a soft SL on pages for non-customer-impacting noise (educational-level pages vs urgent). Where to record this?
- Are there model families that systematically lack runbook mapping? Quick audit needed.

Notes-to-self and informal observations:
- People under pressure default to copy/paste. Anything that reduces manual mapping reduces mistakes.
- Short, visible watchlist in handoffs cut confusion dramatically in my shadow sessions. Keep it short.
- There is a cultural appetite for "small tributes" to reduce noise (eg: a weekly digest of suppressed pages so engineers still know about events).

Next steps (meeting ask):
- Quick 30m sync with eng-sre + eng-platform to agree on 3 priority experiments (alert grouping, handoff template, and SLO-projection) — propose Tue 2027-02-22 09:00 PST.
- Add above action items to JIRA epic SRE-ops-2027-q1-experiments and assign.

Appendix (links & quick references):
- Latency runbook: CONFLUENCE-Runbooks-SRE-Alerting
- Autoscaler incident replay: JIRA-SRE-7894
- Recent pager history: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/playbooks/pull/92

End (notes captured live; will iterate after team sync).
